docs: the race detector runs locally, and CI is a second sample (#61)
The §2 entry was written on a machine with no C toolchain and framed CI as the
only place `mise run test-race` could run. That is no longer where things stand:
the Windows development machine has gcc 16.1.0 (MinGW-w64, x86_64-posix-seh),
CGO_ENABLED is 1 and CC is gcc, so the check is available before a push rather
than only after one.

Measured rather than assumed: `go test -race -count=1 ./...` on 2026-08-14, so
nothing came from the test cache. No data race across all 29 packages that have
tests; two to three minutes wall-clock, of which internal/ui/oci_resources (47 s)
and internal/scan (33 s) are most of it. The entry's "17 packages" was the first
CI run and had gone stale on its own.

CI keeping it is not redundant, and the entry now says why rather than leaving it
to look like duplication: a race is a scheduling accident, so a second machine
with a different core count and scheduler is a second sample, and CI is what
covers a contributor whose machine has no toolchain.

What the entry is actually about survives the rename: the detector only sees code
the tests execute, coverage is 80.7 %, and Rule 110 violations in untested paths
are invisible whichever machine runs it. That is the part that is still debt, so
the heading now names it instead of naming a toolchain problem that is solved.

`.claude/CLAUDE.md` is left alone: "test-race needs cgo and therefore a C
compiler on PATH" is a setup requirement and is still true on a fresh machine.



Entire-Checkpoint: 206078b312ee

Co-authored-by: anthnel <anthnel@proton.me>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
fix: a picker entry is identified by itself, not by its URL (D40) (#60)
The registry browser keyed its selection map on the entry URL, at seven sites:
buildEntries wrote selectedRegs[e.URL], the space handler read and wrote it,
groupState and toggleGroup walked it, submitSearch tested it, the view rendered
it, and Deselected() returned URLs — which is also what browser-selection.json
persists.

Two registries declared on one host is something the form accepts: RegistryForm
enforces slug uniqueness, not URL uniqueness. So ticking either ticked both,
and unchecking either excluded both — for good, since the exclusion is what
survives the session. §3.8 moved entry identity to the slug and said two
registries with the same URL no longer collide; that was true of matching a
discovery result, and the selection map was not carried with it.

browserRegistryEntry now carries a key, and every site reads it through one
selected(entry) accessor rather than indexing the map itself. Seven lookups
free to pick their own identity is how this happened once already.

The key is the slug for a standalone registry, and memberKey(groupSlug,
memberURL) for a member. Neither half is arbitrary. Slug alone will not do —
a member carries its group's, so a whole group would share one checkbox, which
is the trap §1.3 flagged. And within a group the members are told apart by URL
rather than by alias: cleanMemberAlias strips -proxy, -hosted and -local, so
docker-io-proxy and docker-io-hosted both display as docker-io. §3.18 changes
what distinguishes a member — one host, a repo_prefix each — and memberKey is
the one place that has to follow.

browser-selection.json keeps its shape; only what the strings mean changes. An
exclusion written by an earlier build is a URL, matches no key, and the entry
arrives checked. No migration, deliberately: the file records what a user
unticked in a picker, and handing it back over-selected costs one keystroke
where guessing wrong costs a silent omission from every search.

Two tests were written first and both fail on the pre-fix code — one on the
checkbox, one on the exclusion surviving a close and a reopen, which is the
half that outlives the session. TestGroupMembersKeepIndependentCheckboxes
passed before the fix as well as after: it pins the property the obvious key
would have broken, not the defect.

entryFor(url) is deliberately left alone. It resolves a result rather than an
entry and collides the same way, but it is unreachable today — a search over
two entries on one host queries the same URL twice — and it is §3.18 that makes
it live, since a result would then have to carry the prefix to be attributable
at all. It is recorded in that entry's scope table.

Co-authored-by: anthnel <anthnel@proton.me>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
fix: the status view stops advertising settings it does not own (#59)
Three refresh controls in the status header, and none of them was still the
view's to offer.

`±` was already dead. The +/- interval adjustment was removed when the
configuration view took over `status.refresh_interval` — the handler went, and
`TestTheRefreshIntervalIsNotEditableHere` locks it — but the label in
`GetShortcuts()` survived. The header has been promising a key that does
nothing ever since, which is worse than the binding it replaced: a user
pressing it gets no interval change and no reason.

`space` still worked, and that is the problem. It toggled `paused` in memory
only, so the running value and `status.auto_refresh` could disagree and the
toggle was lost on restart — the same shape as the interval it outlived, and
as `gitlab.url` in two views: one setting, two holders, one of which does not
persist.

`ctrl+r` stays. Forcing a check now is an action, not a setting, and Rule 111
makes it a global binding present in every other view; removing it here would
leave no way to refresh and would single this view out.

The field is renamed `paused` -> `autoRefresh` and reads `cfg.Status.AutoRefresh`
directly instead of inverting it. A field called `paused` with no pause action
misnames its only writer, and the inversion is what made the constructor read
`paused: !cfg.Status.AutoRefresh` — one negation between the setting and the
behaviour, for nothing.

`handleRefreshControls` had one case left, so it is `handleManualRefresh` with
no switch. `" "` leaves the key switch in `Update()` and is inert.

The two tests for the toggle are replaced by the two that say it is gone,
mirroring the pair that already existed for the interval:
`TestAutoRefreshIsNotToggleableHere` asserts `space` changes nothing and issues
no command, `TestAutoRefreshComesFromTheConfiguration` that the value has one
source. `TestHelpDocumentsTheAdvertisedShortcuts` loses its `±`/`?` exemption,
which was only ever there because `±` was rendered as "+/-" in the help — all
eight remaining shortcuts are documented as written.

git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat: the dashboard stops reflowing, and gains resource charts (§3.19)

The dashboard laid itself out from whatever the model happened to hold, so it
reflowed on every refresh: a box grew a line when a counter arrived, the row
below moved, and the cursor was somewhere else by the time it was read. It now
has a skeleton — three paliers chosen from the terminal's two dimensions, boxes
whose height is *measured* from the sections they carry, and charts that take
what the skeleton leaves.

Measured, not derived, and that is the whole of it. `gridHeight` and `fitCharts`
render a copy and count its lines rather than consulting a constant; three
constants describing box heights went stale in two days, once per line added.
The router's viewport does not scroll — nothing forwards it a key — so a layout
one line too tall loses that line in silence, which is the failure this replaces.

`internal/metrics` is new: a gopsutil host sample (~5 ms) on a one-second tick,
`docker stats` (~2 s) on a five-second one, and the configured slow refresh for
everything that reads a file or an API. Three clocks because one would have to
be the slowest of them. `metrics.Size` walks the workspaces tree for the space
it occupies — 811 ms measured on 2.38 GiB, on its own command, once per slow
round, never concurrent with itself.

The boxes: Health carries the monitors, the certificates and what the scan
caches know (Rule 126 — it reads them, it never scans); Code carries the GitLab
session and the workspaces; Docker (VM) counts; Storage weighs. That last pair
is a rule rather than a coincidence — the same figure appeared in three boxes,
so the workspaces path is Code's alone, free space is Storage's, and the image
and volume sizes moved to Storage while Docker keeps the counts. `docker system
df`'s build-cache row was already parsed and summed into the reclaimable total
with its own size thrown away; it is the line that most often answers where the
disk went, and Storage shows it now.

At `wide` the Health and Docker boxes split into two columns — nineteen lines
became eleven, which is what the three charts above them get back. `sideBySide`
pads and joins by hand: lipgloss does not inherit a background (Rule 115), so
`JoinHorizontal` would print the terminal's own between the columns.

`internal/ui/theme/box.go` draws the frames, and the router grew a second resize
pass: a view whose footer height depends on its palier cannot answer before it
knows its size, so the first pass tells it and the second asks.

Two defects found by review rather than by use: `truncatePath` sliced bytes and
cut accented paths mid-rune, and `failureCount` printed a check mark beside a
`down` count of zero. Both have a test that fails on the code they replace, as
do the two layout guards — the column gutter, and the second trees of a split
box opening on the same line.
EOF
